headline: Council approves Resolution 2026-19 updating no-parking areas, including one-side parking on East Terrace.
summary: The change sets a no-parking ban on one side of East Terrace from 6 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Friday. Public Works will check the street signs to match. Residents who spoke gave mixed views on one-side parking, and some asked for resident-only permits. The council also created a parking fund and approved pension plan changes that the actuaries estimate would set the city's contribution at $889,000, down from a preliminary $992,000.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda except item 6C, which included warrants, parking ticket fees, and minutes, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved Resolution 2026-17 creating a parking fund, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved Resolution 2026-19 updating no-parking areas, including East Terrace, with Monday through Friday hours, by unanimous voice vote.
Approved changes to the actuarial assumptions for the South Burlington pension plan, by unanimous voice vote.
discussion: East Terrace parking: Residents gave mixed views on one-side parking and asked about resident-only permits. Public Works said it would check all signs to make sure they match the new rules.
Parking fund: Members debated whether parking fees should go to a separate fund or the general fund. Staff said it could take a couple of years before parking fees cover the fund's costs.

Pension plan changes: The actuaries said the lower return rate and newer mortality table would raise the plan's accrued liability to $59.9 million. They said the funded level would rise to about 95 percent.

Legislative priorities: Councilors ranked local option tax changes, transportation funding, and other ideas for the state session. Staff will bring three to five priorities back to the council at its next meeting.
Graffiti and vacant building ordinance: Members discussed a rule covering graffiti, broken windows, and vacant buildings. Staff said the item is low on its list, and members set it aside for later.
